jobs.title: Principal Kernel & Device Drivers Engineer
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the role
 SambaNova is seeking a Principal Engineer to own kernel-level drivers and low-level software for high-speed IO, memory, and networking subsystems within the DataScale® platform and RDU architecture. This role is central to delivering reliable, high-performance AI systems at scale. This is a hands-on Linux kernel and device driver role; it is not an application or platform software role.

You will lead software bring-up of new silicon, deliver production drivers across the IO, memory, and network data paths, and debug complex issues spanning kernel, firmware, and hardware. This role suits an engineer with deep kernel and driver expertise and strong hardware fluency, who can operate in ambiguity and execute with high ownership.

Responsibilities

  • Own kernel-space drivers for high-speed IO, memory, and networking subsystems, from architecture through production release
  • Own the RDMA and network data path, including queue-pair management, congestion control, QoS, and packet classification
  • Lead software enablement for platform bring-up across new silicon and system configurations
  • Drive issues to root cause across kernel, firmware, and hardware layers with hardware, firmware, and validation teams
  • Own PHY and link bring-up in coordination with hardware teams, working from specifications and register documentation
  • Build tools, test scripts, and frameworks for device and NIC verification, performance analysis, and manufacturing test
  • Identify and resolve bottlenecks across driver, network stack, and system layers at data center scale
  • Set code quality standards through design and code review, and mentor engineers on the team

Required Qualifications

  • MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
  • 7+ years of experience in kernel or low-level system software development
  • Deep expertise in Linux systems programming and kernel driver development
  • Strong knowledge of Linux kernel networking, including network driver development and the RDMA protocol
  • Strong C/C++ programming and debugging skills, with scripting in Python or shell
  • Experience with two or more high-speed IO or interconnect technologies such as PCIe, Ethernet, or CXL
  • Proven ability to lead hardware-software co-debug from first silicon to production
  • Ability to read and distill hardware specifications and register-level documentation
  • Clear and effective communicator with a proactive, collaborative approach to problem-solving

  • Experience with virtual switching and data center networking at scale

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's go-to-market teams are scaling quickly, and the decisions they make, from who to sell to and how to cover them to where to invest next, are only as good as the intelligence and infrastructure underneath them. As a Data Engineer on the GTM Systems data foundations team, you'll help build that layer: the data products that give sellers, operators, and analysts a rich, current, and trusted picture of the market, and the engineering rigor that lets our GTM systems run reliably as the business grows.

This is an engineering role that goes beyond pipelines. You'll treat GTM data as a product and a platform: built once, kept current, and available wherever people work. Alongside the build, you'll help shape what the data means: how attributes are defined, which sources are trusted, and how the business puts them to use. The role sits at the intersection of the sales organization, the data organization, and the systems that data flows through. You'll partner closely with Sales Strategy and Operations, Finance, Data Science, and the central data engineering team.

Key responsibilities

  • Bring disparate internal and external sources together: orchestrate, model, and normalize first-party product and revenue data alongside third-party data into one usable understanding of the company landscape

  • Build and maintain identity and entity resolution, so every source attaches to one trusted record for each company and the relationships between companies are clear

  • Help build the canonical layer where key attributes are defined once and mean the same thing everywhere, with clear sourcing logic, provenance, and freshness

  • Turn data into intelligence: scores, signals, and AI-generated attributes that help GTM teams prioritize and act, held to the same quality bar as any other source

  • Deliver that intelligence to the surfaces where teams work, including the CRM, and bring production discipline to how data moves through those systems

  • Operate what you build as a living system, with observability, data quality, cost, security, and access controls designed in, so problems surface before the field sees them

  • Partner with the owners of GTM processes such as planning, segmentation, and routing to settle definitions, make clear commitments, and communicate tradeoffs

  • Make the platform easy for other teams to build on, so work is contributed once and not rebuilt in silos

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience as a data engineer or analytics engineer building and operating production pipelines and data models

  • Strong SQL and Python, and experience with modern transformation and orchestration tooling on a cloud data warehouse

  • Experience making messy data from many sources usable, including record matching, deduplication, and reconciling conflicting values

  • Familiarity with go-to-market data and the CRM systems it flows through

  • Clear written and verbal communication with technical and non-technical partners

  • Regular hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering work

  • 5+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, or GTM data roles

jobs.title: Senior Validation & SI Correlation Engineer
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the Role

SambaNova Systems is redefining what’s possible in AI infrastructure—and the hardware that powers it has to be flawless. As a Senior Hardware Validation & SI Correlation Engineer, you will own the technical bridge between simulation and silicon, ensuring that every high-speed link, control bus, and power rail in our next-generation AI server systems performs without compromise.

This is a high-impact, highly visible role that blends deep Signal Integrity (SI) expertise with rigorous system-level hardware validation. You will work at the frontier of AI compute—validating PCIe Gen5/6, DDR5, and 112G/224G Ethernet interfaces on systems pushing the limits of what data center hardware can do. If you thrive in a fast-paced lab environment, love digging into root cause, and want your work to directly accelerate the future of AI, this role is built for you.

What You’ll Do

SI Modeling & Measurement Correlation

  • Drive the correlation between pre- and post-layout SI simulations and physical lab measurements, closing the loop between theory and hardware reality.
  • Quantify simulation-vs-measurement gaps for PCIe Gen5/6, DDR5, and 112G/224G Ethernet using S-parameters, TDR, and eye diagram analysis.
  • Develop and refine EM models for PCB discontinuities, high-speed connectors, and vias using Ansys HFSS, Cadence Sigrity, or equivalent tools.
  • Investigate discrepancies caused by manufacturing tolerances, material properties (Dk/Df), or de-embedding inaccuracies and drive them to resolution.

System-Level Electrical Validation

  • Lead validation of housekeeping and control buses—I2C, SPI, eSPI, UART, SMBus—ensuring protocol compliance and robust timing margins.
  • Validate complex power-on/off sequences and correlate VR control loop simulations with physical transient response and ripple measurements.
  • Ensure reliable operation of sideband signals, reset logic, and BMC hardware interfaces under intensive AI workloads.
  • Work cross-functionally with SI, Power Integrity (PI), and Firmware teams to resolve system-hang and link-training failures rooted in electrical noise or power instability.

Test Methodology & Automation

  • Author comprehensive Hardware Validation Plans (HVP) with full coverage of critical electrical test points.
  • Build Python-based automation scripts to drive data collection from VNAs, BERTs, and oscilloscopes—accelerating validation throughput and repeatability.

What You’ll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering (M.S. preferred).
  • 10+ years of experience in high-speed digital design or hardware validation within a data center, systems architecture, or server bring-up environment.
  • Expert-level proficiency in SI/EM tools: Ansys HFSS/SIwave, Cadence Sigrity/Allegro, or Keysight ADS.
  • Hands-on mastery of high-bandwidth real-time oscilloscopes, VNAs, and logic analyzers.
  • Deep knowledge of high-speed protocol physical layers (PCIe, IEEE 802.3) and low-spee

Titre du poste: Ingénieur en intelligence artificielle (IA)

Description du poste

Nous sommes à la recherche d'un(e) ingénieur(e) en intelligence artificielle hautement qualifié(e) pour concevoir et développer des applications alimentées par l'IA de calibre production au sein d'un environnement d'entreprise à grande échelle. Ce rôle soutient des initiatives au sein de l'une des plus importantes organisations d'assurance aux États-Unis, visant à transformer l'expérience des membres grâce à l'intelligence artificielle.

L'équipe développe actuellement un assistant basé sur l'IA pour soutenir le traitement des réclamations, ainsi qu'une plateforme intégrée à 360° permettant de créer des profils de santé complets pour les utilisateurs. Ces solutions s'appuient sur des capacités avancées de grands modèles de langage (LLM) et sont soutenues par une vaste plateforme de découverte et d'exploitation des données.

Responsabilités
• Contribuer à la conception et à la mise en uvre de solutions d'IA agentique, notamment pour des cas d'utilisation tels que les jumeaux numériques et les systèmes intelligents destinés aux membres.
• Concevoir et développer des flux de travail LLM agentiques ou multiétapes de niveau production, incluant la logique d'orchestration et la coordination entre plusieurs composantes d'IA ou services backend.
• Définir l'architecture système à partir de zéro.
• Concevoir, développer et intégrer des API RESTful tout en contribuant au développement frontend et backend.
• Maintenir des pratiques d'ingénierie de niveau production en matière de conteneurisation, de tests, de performance, d'évolutivité et de fiabilité à l'aide de Docker.
• Participer à des discussions orientées solutions avec les parties prenantes.

Compétences essentielles
• Expérience avec les architectures sans serveur (Serverless) sur AWS et le développement de systèmes de production utilisant AWS Lambda, Amazon Bedrock, API Gateway et DynamoDB.
• Expertise en Infrastructure as Code (IaC) avec CloudFormation ou Terraform.
• Expérience en développement full stack et en conception d'API.
• Maîtrise des pratiques d'ingénierie de niveau production.
• Solides compétences en communication et expérience auprès des clients ou des parties prenantes.

Compétences et qualifications supplémentaires
• Expérience dans un environnement réglementé par la HIPAA.
• Bonne connaissance ou expérience significative de développement en Python.
• Expérience dans les secteurs de la santé ou du gouvernement.

Environnement de travail

Le travail à distance est possible partout au Canada ou aux États-Unis, à l'exception du Québec. jobs.title: Senior/Staff System Research Engineer – LLM Inference Optimization
jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.
We are looking for talented systems developers and researchers to join the Snowflake AI Research team and advance the state of the art in LLM inference systems and optimization.

Our mission is to build the next generation of high-performance and intelligent inference systems. We optimize not only how fast and efficiently models run, but also how quickly inference systems can adapt to new models, architectures, hardware, and workloads.

Our work spans the full inference stack—from distributed serving and runtime systems to GPU kernels and model-system co-design. We explore techniques such as adaptive parallelism, speculative and parallel decoding, disaggregated inference, scheduling and batching, KV-cache optimization, model swapping, quantization, and GPU kernel optimization to push the frontier of latency, throughput, scalability, and cost.

Beyond optimizing individual models, we are building intelligent and adaptive inference systems that can automate performance optimization—rapidly profiling new models and workloads, identifying bottlenecks, selecting effective execution strategies, and adapting system configurations with minimal manual tuning. We embrace AI-native engineering, using AI not only as the workload we optimize, but also as a tool to accelerate system development, experimentation, debugging, optimization, and adaptation to new models. Our goal is to accelerate both the speed of inference and the agility of inference development.

This is an exciting opportunity to collaborate with a world-class team, including founding members of DeepSpeed, vLLM, and TensorFlow. Together, we will push the boundaries of AI systems and bring cutting-edge research into production-scale AI.

Responsibilities
• Design and develop high-performance LLM inference systems, spanning distributed serving, runtime systems, GPU execution, and performance-critical kernels.

• Develop novel techniques to improve inference latency, generation speed, throughput, memory efficiency, scalability, and cost.

• Explore advanced inference techniques including speculative and parallel decoding, prefill/decode disaggregation, adaptive parallelism, continuous batching and scheduling, KV-cache management, quantization, and communication optimization.

• Develop adaptive and intelligent inference systems that automatically optimize execution for new model architectures, hardware platforms, workload characteristics, and deployment environments.

• Apply AI-driven and AI-native approaches to systems engineering, including automated profiling, bottleneck identification, configuration search, code generation, experimentation, runtime strategy selection, debugging, and performance tuning.

• Independently identify high-impact performance and systems problems, formulate hypotheses, prototype solutions, and drive promising ideas from research through production.

• Design distributed inference strategies across GPUs and nodes, including tensor, sequence, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism.

• Develop efficient approaches for multi-model serving, dynamic resource management, model loading and swapping, and workload-aware scheduling.

• Analyze and optimize GPU kernels and operators for attention, MoE, communication, and other performance-critical model components.

PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture and customer support of high-quality light-, medium- and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates. We're the only platform they need to stay ahead of tech trends and news, develop their careers and find opportunities at companies they believe in.Our 1,800 customers include innovative companies of all sizes, from exciting startups to companies in the Fortune 100. This helps them hire the industry's most sought-after professionals locally, nationally and remotely - ultimately contributing to the industry's ability to innovate a better future.

What You'll Be a Part Of

Working at Built In is the chance to help shape a fast-growing company. With venture funding of $30 million to date, we're expanding not just our geographic footprint but our products and technology. You'll also be a part of changing the lives of professionals like you, ambitious people with a passion for tech and love of learning. As a result, you'll understand the impact of your work in a deeply personal, especially meaningful way.

We are looking for an Applied AI Engineer to design and build the autonomous systems that power Built In's product suite. Our platform already generates deep analytical insights for customers—your job is to build the Agentic Action Layer that turns those insights into outcomes. You will create multi-agent systems that don't just surface data but take intelligent, supervised action across the major AI frontiers: ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Perplexity.

• Architect Agentic Systems: Design and implement production-grade agentic workflows—including Reflection, Self-Correction, Planning, and Multi-Agent Orchestration patterns to power a growing portfolio of AI-driven product capabilities.

• Collaborate Across Teams: Work closely with Software Engineers and Product Managers to integrate agentic behaviors into production frameworks, ensuring AI systems are stateful, observable, and resilient.

What You Bring

• 5+ years of full-time professional software engineering experience . Internships, training programs and academic projects are valuable but don't count toward this.

• Agentic systems you've shipped to production, for an employer or for customers . Patterns like ReAct, Planning, Reflection, and Multi-Agent Orchestration. You've moved agents from demo to production and dealt with the hard parts: failure handling, state management, and non-deterministic outputs.

• Evaluation you've built and relied on. Custom evaluation frameworks such as LLM-as-a-Judge, trace-based testing and regression suites, used to keep agent output quality up over time. You understand that the hardest part of production agents isn't building them. It's knowing when they're wrong.

• Hands-on work with frontier model APIs from OpenAI, Google, Perplexity or Anthropic, including function calling, structured outputs, and streaming.

• Strong Python for AI orchest

You'll drive a high-impact research agenda focused on large language models, agentic reasoning, and the system-level capabilities that make AI genuinely useful at enterprise scale. This is a rare opportunity to do research that matters twice over — advancing the field and shipping directly into products used by hundreds of thousands of people every day.

We're at an inflection point. Enterprises are moving from experimenting with AI to deeply embedding it across their operations, and WRITER's models are the engine making that possible. The work you do here — on post-training, planning, multi-step reasoning, and agentic workflows — will directly shape how the next generation of enterprise AI behaves, performs, and scales. You'll have the resources, infrastructure, and cross-functional support to pursue ambitious ideas and bring them to life quickly. This role is hybrid, based out of our San Francisco or New York City hub.

 - Lead an independent, high-impact research agenda on large language models and agentic systems, owning projects from early hypothesis through model training, evaluation, and production deployment

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Distributed Storage and HPC & AI Infrastructure
jobs.description:
About the Role

In this role, you will operate, scale, and optimize multi-petabyte storage systems purpose-built for the world’s largest AI training and inference workloads. Storage now sits on the inference critical path as well, so you’ll also build the caching and data-movement layers that deliver KV cache and model weights directly into GPU memory at fabric speed. You’ll manage and scale high-performance parallel filesystems and object stores, evaluate and integrate cutting-edge technologies such as Vast, Weka, Ceph, and Lustre, and solve the complex engineering challenges of operating at extreme throughput, low-latency data paths, and massive cluster-scale storage operations. 

You will also build Kubernetes-native storage operators and self-service platforms that provide automated provisioning, strict multi-tenancy, performance isolation, and quota enforcement at cluster scale. Day-to-day, you’ll optimize end-to-end data paths for 10-50 GB/s per node, design multi-tier caching architectures, implement intelligent prefetching and model-weight distribution, build KV-cache offload and reuse tiers for inference, and tune parallel filesystems for AI workloads. 

Responsibilities

  • Architect and implement the technical strategy and storage roadmap for Together AI, driving high-performance architectural decisions as we scale our GPU fleet.
  • Engineer and scale multi-petabyte AI/ML storage systems by integrating Vast, Weka, and Ceph while executing deep cost optimization through automated tiering and lifecycle policies.
  • Develop intelligent caching and tiered storage architectures to achieve extreme IOPS and cluster-wide throughput at GPU scale for training and inference workloads, including GPU-direct (RDMA) delivery of model weights for fast cold starts and autoscaling.
  • Design and build KV-cache offload and reuse for inference: tiering KV blocks across GPU HBM, host memory, local NVMe, and distributed cache, enabling prefix reuse across requests and nodes, and integrating with inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) to cut time-to-first-token.
  • Tune storage isolation at the L2/L3 network layers to ensure secure, production-grade multi-tenancy for storage clients.
  • Code Kubernetes storage operators and controllers to enable automated provisioning, self-service abstractions, and quota enforcement.
  • Engineer end-to-end data paths to achieve 10+ GB/s per GPU node; architect multi-tier caching for model weights, KV cache, and datasets; tune parallel filesystems using advanced profiling; and scale storage infrastructure across thousands of nodes.
  • Optimize end-to-end data paths through advanced benchmarking and profiling, contributing high-impact code to open-source storage and inference projects and internal tooling.

Requirements

  • 8+ years in storage engineering, managing distributed storage at multi-petabyte scale
  • Proven track record building, deploying and operating high-performance storage for GPU/HPC clusters, for training and/or inference
  • Experience scaling storage for inference: KV-cache offload or disaggregated KV storage, prefix caching, model-weight distribution, or similar latency-critical data paths
  • Deep Kubernetes and cloud-native storage experience in production environments
  • Strong coding skills in Go and Python with demonstrated ability to build production-grade systems and tooling
  • BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
  • History of technical leadership: designing systems that significantly improved performance, reliability (99.999%+ uptime), or cost efficiency
  • Distributed Storage Systems: Deep expertise in either of Ceph, WekaFS, Lustre, Vast, GPFS, or similar parallel filesystems at multi-petabyte scale

This is a creator role. You are a technical storyteller. You'll produce social-native posts, technical blogs, performance benchmarks, demo and explainer videos, and thought leadership, all aimed at one outcome: building Together’s credibility with developers. jobs.title: AI Automation Engineer

GAQ427R224

We're hiring an AI Automation Engineer to build the next generation of IT automations to improve the employee experience at Databricks.

You'll be building production-grade AI agents and automation services that understand employee requests, retrieve enterprise context, reason across systems, invoke tools and APIs, and take action safely. The goal isn't to automate existing workflows the same way we've done it for the past decade. It's to reimagine how employees interact with IT through intelligent, contextual, and increasingly agentic experiences and to do it on Databricks.

What you will do

  • Build AI agents and automations: Design, deploy, and run AI agents that support all of our employees. The agents interpret natural-language requests, gather context, select tools, execute actions, and communicate outcomes.
  • Maintain MCP servers across our AI tools portfolio.
  • Build agentic workflows that decompose goals into steps, handle failures, pause for human approval as needed, and resume their workflows.
  • Ground agents in trusted internal knowledge (policies, runbooks, system documentation, SOPs, etc).
  • Turn high-volume support CUJs into self-service experiences: Identify repetitive, high-friction IT interactions and convert them into reliable AI automation experiences.
  • Instrument AI automations with logs, metrics, and feedback loops.
  • Design and implement AI automations with identity governance, tools RBAC, human-in-the-loop approvals where applicable, audit trails, and failure handling.
  • Create shared automation infrastructure (credential vaults, event ingestion, scheduling, approval workflows, cache/state stores) that other teams can build on.
  • Work with IT Support, Employee Experience, Security, IAM, Infrastructure, and Engineering to identify automation opportunities and take solutions from prototype to production.
  • Write and maintain high-quality technical/engineering documentation that clearly communicates system designs, operational procedures, and architectural decisions.

What we are looking for

  • Proficiency in Python or Go [3yrs].
  • Experience with Git-based development, automated testing, and CI/CD.
  • Strong experience with REST APIs, OAuth2/authentication frameworks, event-driven integrations, and enterprise system integrations.
  • Shipped production LLM-powered applications or AI agents.
  • Experience with agent patterns: tool/function calling, multi-step workflows, context management, RAG, structured outputs, and plan decomposition.
  • Understanding of LLM failure modes: hallucination, incorrect tool use, ambiguous intent, prompt injection, excessive permissions, and non-deterministic behavior.
  • Experience evaluating and improving AI systems using automated evals, traces, test datasets, human feedback, or similar approaches.
  • Ability to translate ambiguous employee friction problems into simple, reliable technical solutions.
  • Strong judgment around security, privacy, least privilege, and safe automation in an enterprise environment.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills. You will work cross-functionally to plan, design, and implement automation together.
  • Experience with automation or integration platforms (Tines, MuleSoft, Workato, etc.).
  • Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) server development.

Nice to have

  • Experience building agents on Databricks (Agent Bricks) or with frameworks such as OpenAI Agents SDK or LangGraph/LangChain.
  • Experience with MLflow tracing/evaluation, vector search, and LLM observability.
  • Experience integrating IT platforms: Okta/Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Jira, Slack, Jamf, GitHub, Workd

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As an early member of our Finance Analytics and Business Intelligence team, you will play an instrumental role in our company's mission of building safe and beneficial artificial intelligence by establishing robust analytics engineering and business intelligence capabilities for our Finance & Accounting organization. In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to ensuring accurate financial reporting, streamlining accounting processes, and supporting our financial operations as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world.

As a founding Data Scientist on Anthropic's Finance Forecasting team, you'll own revenue forecasting models that drive capacity planning and board reporting, build the backtesting and accuracy discipline that makes those forecasts trustworthy, and lead causal measurement work that tells us how much a given launch or event actually moved revenue — turning what is currently a best-guess conversation into a designed, repeatable readout.

We're hiring for two seats on this team, and we expect candidates to lead with depth in either production time-series forecasting or causal inference. Both shapes are first-class; tell us in your application which one feels more like you.

This is a build role on a small team. The forecast is visible inside the company, and when it's wrong, people notice. We're looking for someone who would rather have their models scored than stay vague, and who is excited to set the bar for how forecasting is done here.

Key responsibilities

  • Own a core piece of the team's modeling work — either the production revenue forecasts themselves (scoping, development, backtesting, deployment, monitoring) or the causal measurement program for launches and events

  • Contribute to the team's broader research direction, including event-aware forecast architectures, hierarchical reconciliation, and causal designs that hold up under launch-driven step-changes

jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the Team

The Machine Learning team builds the model-side techniques that make SambaNova’s platform fast and capable. We train speculative decoding models that accelerate inference, develop efficient ML methods such as quantization, sparsity, and distillation, and build agentic systems on top of our foundation model serving stack. Our work spans research, applied science, and production, from novel approach design to proofs of concept and shipping to product. Reinforcement learning and post-training are within our scope and a growing part of our roadmap.

About the Role

As a new grad Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll train and evaluate models that make large language models cheaper and more capable to serve. Depending on your interests, that could mean training speculator (draft) models and tuning acceptance rates, compressing models without losing accuracy, or designing and evaluating agentic workflows for tool use, planning, and long-horizon tasks. You’ll work closely with the AI performance, compiler, and runtime teams to turn research results into measured end-to-end wins, and you’ll have room to pursue open problems as our reinforcement learning and post-training work ramps up.

Responsibilities

  • Train, evaluate, and tune speculative decoding models (Dspark/Dflash, Medusa/Eagle-style heads, and multi-token prediction) to increase acceptance rates on production workloads.
  • Develop and implement optimization techniques, including quantization, sparsity, distillation, pruning, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, to quantify the trade-offs between model quality, latency, and resource efficiency.
  • Build and evaluate agentic systems: tool calling, multi-step planning, retrieval, and long-context reasoning on top of our serving stack.
  • Design rigorous evaluations and benchmarks; make accuracy and quality claims that hold up under scrutiny
  • Translate recent research into working implementations, and run ablations to understand what actually drives the result
  • Partner with the AI performance, compiler, runtime, and product teams to ship model improvements into SambaNova products
  • Contribute to emerging areas such as reinforcement learning, post-training, and reward modeling as the roadmap expands

Required Qualifications

  • B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
  • Strong programming skills in Python
  • Solid foundation in machine learning, linear algebra, probability, and numerical computing
  • Hands-on experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX

  • Ability to design a clean experiment, interpret results honestly, and communicate findings clearly

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
  • Research or internship experience in LLM training, post-training, or inference
  • Experience with speculative decoding, distillation, quantization, sparsity, or other model efficiency techniques
  • Experience building agentic systems, tool-calling pipe

This role owns a portfolio, not a single program. That portfolio may include skills verification, technical validation, role-based readiness paths, practical challenges, and new approaches we have not yet imagined. Your job is to understand where the field is headed, identify the capabilities that will matter most, and turn that insight into experiences and systems that help FEs grow and perform.

This is a high-visibility, high-autonomy role for someone who wants to build. You will work with FE leaders, product and technical communities, regional teams, enablement partners, HR, and internal platform teams to define what “field-ready” means and make it useful in the flow of work. You will have the opportunity to influence how a global technical organization develops - and to create programs that become part of how Databricks operates.

The best person for this role is equal parts strategist, product thinker, builder, and operator. You can see around corners, create structure from ambiguity, earn trust with senior stakeholders, and turn an idea into something the field actually uses. You are energized by the possibility of using AI not only as a topic to teach, but as a catalyst to redesign how capability is built, measured, and scaled.

What You'll Do

  • Set the vision and roadmap for FE capability. Develop a clear point of view on how Databricks should build, demonstrate, recognize, and continuously evolve field expertise. Translate FE strategy, product priorities, customer needs, and the changing nature of technical work into a focused portfolio of investments.
  • Own and evolve a portfolio of readiness experiences. Bring together existing programs and new opportunities across skills verification, technical demonstrations, role-based pathways, credentials, and practical application. Decide what to scale, redesign, connect, or retire to keep the portfolio coherent and valuable.
  • Invent new ways for FEs to build and prove expertise. When the field needs a new capability, design the right experience - not automatically another course. This could be a customer scenario, a live technical demonstration, a peer review, a contribution model, an AI-enabled assessment, or something entirely new. Prototype quickly, learn from the field, and scale the strongest ideas.
  • Make readiness relevant to the work FEs actually do. Partner with practitioners, managers, product teams, and SME communities to define credible standards and evidence of capability. Embed development and validation into existing FE workflows wherever possible, making readiness a pull-based experience rather than an additional layer of process.
  • Help the organization adapt to an AI-enabled future. Stay close to how AI is changing FE workflows, technical depth, customer engagement, and delivery models. Experiment with AI to improve assessment quality, personalize development, surface expertise, and scale program operations responsibly.

jobs.title: Senior Network Engineer (Amsterdam)
jobs.description:
About the Role

Together AI is looking for a Senior Network Engineer to design, deploy, and operate the global network infrastructure supporting our production services and high-performance AI compute environments.

This is a hands-on engineering role for someone with deep networking expertise who can also troubleshoot across Linux, Kubernetes, automation, and application boundaries. You will work on large-scale, multi-vendor data center networks and help ensure they remain highly available, reliable, scalable, and performant.

The ideal candidate has strong networking fundamentals, experience operating complex networks at scale, and a structured, evidence-based approach to troubleshooting. You should be comfortable owning problems from initial investigation through root cause and resolution, including situations where the issue may extend beyond the network itself.

Responsibilities

  • Design, deploy, operate, and maintain global, multi-vendor, multi-protocol networks supporting high-performance AI compute infrastructure.
  • Troubleshoot complex network and application-connectivity issues, identify root causes, and drive problems through resolution.
  • Analyze telemetry, packet captures, logs, and performance data to identify network degradation, congestion, packet loss, and capacity constraints.
  • Participate in architecture and design reviews to ensure solutions meet requirements for performance, availability, scalability, security, and operational supportability.
  • Develop and maintain automation, validation, and operational tooling that improves network reliability and reduces manual effort.
  • Evaluate network hardware, software, optics, and emerging technologies for use in production environments.
  • Establish standards and operational best practices for network design, deployment, monitoring, change management, and incident response.
  • Lead projects addressing complex technical challenges and contribute directly to the network engineering roadmap.
  • Partner with infrastructure, systems, security, and application teams to troubleshoot issues that cross traditional ownership boundaries.

Requirements

  • 8+ years of professional experience designing, building, and supporting large-scale production data center, cloud, service-provider, or high-performance computing networks (excluding enterprise networks).
  • Must have hands-on experience deploying or operating RoCE and/or InfiniBand fabrics.
  • Deep understanding of TCP/IP and strong experience with technologies such as BGP, OSPF, VXLAN, EVPN, ECMP, and QoS.
  • Experience designing and supporting multi-tenant network environments using technologies such as VRFs, VLANs, overlays, and policy-based segmentation.
  • Hands-on experience deploying and troubleshooting network platforms from vendors such as Arista, Cisco, Juniper, and NVIDIA.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills using tools such as Wireshark, tcpdump, MTR, curl, nmap, and standard Linux networking utilities.
  • Ability to diagnose connectivity, latency, packet-loss, routing, and performance issues across the network, host, and application layers.
  • Experience developing or maintaining network automation using Python, Ansible, or similar tools.
  • Experience working through a Git-based software development lifecycle, including branching, code review, validation, linting, testing, CI/CD, deployment, and rollback.
  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes networking, including pods, services, CNIs, and basic connectivity troubleshooting.
  • Foundational knowledge of RDMA networking and technologies such as RoCE or InfiniBand.
  • Experience with cloud networking in AWS, GCP, or Azure.
  • Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting skills.</

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Benchmarks & Evaluation
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT RAMP LABS

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Every model decision at Ramp Labs runs through a benchmark. Which model to route to. Whether a post-training run worked. Whether an agent is ready to post a corrective journal entry to a customer's ledger without a human in the loop.

You'll own Ramp's benchmarking effort. You'll turn real finance work (expense policy review, invoice coding, month-end close, spreadsheet Q&A) into benchmarks and RL environments, build the graders, and tell the team what is actually improving.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build benchmarks from real workflows: turn agent traces, customer edge cases and expert labels into versioned benchmark suites for long-horizon agents that run for hours across tools and systems, plus tool use, multi-step reasoning and financial judgment

 - Own the benchmarking effort: decide what we measure, run benchmark suites across models and agent versions, and report results the team makes decisions on

 - Design graders: rubrics, programmatic checks and llm-as-judge, calibrated against human agreement, with a clear view of where each one breaks

 - Close the loop with post-training: turn evals into reward functions and RL environments, and catch reward hacking and contamination before they ship

 - Publish external benchmarks and write-ups on how models perform at real finance work




WHAT YOU NEED

 - Hands-on experience building LLM benchmarks or evals that people used to make real decisions

 - Strong Python and software engineering; your eval code is reproducible and fast

 - Statistical judgment: variance, confidence intervals, sample size, inter-rater agreement, and knowing when a delta is noise

 - Working knowledge of post-training (SFT, RL with verifiable rewards) and how evals feed into it

 - Comfort with SQL and large datasets; you'll work directly from production traces

 - Taste for what is worth measuring




NICE-TO-HAVE

 - Industry experience on an eval, benchmarking or post-training team

 - Built RL environments or verifiers for agentic tasks

 - Published benchmark or evaluation research (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICML, ACL)

 - Built or contributed to eval frameworks (verifiers, lm-evaluation-harness, HELM or similar)

 - Familiarity with accounting, finance or other expert-domain work

 - Public work we can look at: a benchmark, an eval suite, a failure-analysis write-up




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial co

jobs.title: (Staff / Senior Staff) AI Inference Reliability Engineer, Compute Infra
jobs.description:
About The Role 

We're looking for a software engineer, reliability-minded but still a builder, to own what happens in production to the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. The platform team builds the manifest-driven API and controllers that let the inference team declare what they need, a cluster, a model deployment, a capacity change, and get it reconciled underneath. Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page.

The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. Strong candidates have hands-on production-reliability experience on large-scale distributed or GPU-serving systems, are comfortable troubleshooting InfiniBand/RDMA and Kubernetes controller/CRD-based platforms, and think about GPU infrastructure, and the tools that keep it reliable, as software to be engineered.

A product mindset applies: the on-call experience, the clarity of an alert, and the judgment built into an automated remediation are things you ship and iterate on.

Responsibilities

  • Operate the provisioning state machine in production: own the health of the host lifecycle pipeline, discovery, inference bring-up, GPU driver/CUDA validation, health checks, decommission/RMA, triaging stuck or failed state transitions at fleet scale and feeding real failure patterns back into how the states and transitions are designed.
  • Triage and extend automated self-healing: when the node-scanning and remediation platform misses something, a new failure mode, an InfiniBand issue in disaggregated prefill/decode serving, a GPU Xid variant, a hero-model or LoRA-specific fault, diagnose it live, drive the fix to production, and turn it into a new detection/remediation plugin so it's automatic the next time.
  • Own end-to-end reliability of the pipeline: hold the SLOs and error budgets for provisioning and fleet health, lead incident response when idempotency, retry, rollback, or drift assumptions break down in practice, and drive the systemic fix, not just the hotfix.
  • Partner with the inference/ML platform team from the production side: be the one who knows how real cluster topologies, interconnects, and scheduling constraints actually fail in the field, and feed those failure modes back as first-class requirements into the platform's abstractions.
  • Work alongside machine learning researchers, engineers, and product managers to bring our latest technologies into production, enabling advanced research through awesome engineering.
  • Introduce new techniques, tools, and architecture that improve the performance, latency, throughput, and efficiency of our model inference stack.
  • Build tools to give us visibility into our bottlenecks and sources of instability, then design and implement solutions to address the highest-priority issues.
  • Lead reliability cross-functionally: build coalition across infra, ML platform, and product teams around shared reliability priorities, manage stakeholders through incidents and roadmap trade-offs, and represent the reliability point of view in planning so it shapes decisions before they ship

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Distributed Storage and HPC & AI Infrastructure
jobs.description:
About the Role

In this role, you will operate, scale, and optimize multi-petabyte storage systems purpose-built for the world’s largest AI training and inference workloads. You’ll manage and scale high-performance parallel filesystems and object stores, evaluate and integrate cutting-edge technologies such as Vast, Weka, Ceph, and Lustre, and solve the complex engineering challenges of operating at extreme throughput, low-latency data paths, and massive cluster-scale storage operations. 

You will also build Kubernetes-native storage operators and self-service platforms that provide automated provisioning, strict multi-tenancy, performance isolation, and quota enforcement at cluster scale. Day-to-day, you’ll optimize end-to-end data paths for 10-50 GB/s per node, design multi-tier caching architectures, implement intelligent prefetching and model-weight distribution, and tune parallel filesystems for AI workloads. 

2 days a week in our office in Amsterdam

Responsibilities

  • Architect and implement the technical strategy and storage roadmap for Together AI, driving high-performance architectural decisions as we scale our GPU fleet.
  • Engineer and scale multi-petabyte AI/ML storage systems by integrating Vast, Weka, and Ceph while executing deep cost optimization through automated tiering and lifecycle policies.
  • Develop intelligent caching and tiered storage architectures to achieve extreme IOPS and cluster-wide throughput at GPU scale for training and inference workloads.
  • Tune storage isolation at the L2/L3 network layers to ensure secure, production-grade multi-tenancy for storage clients.
  • Code Kubernetes storage operators and controllers to enable automated provisioning, self-service abstractions, and quota enforcement.
  • Engineer end-to-end data paths to achieve 10+ GB/s per GPU node; architect multi-tier caching for model weights and datasets; tune parallel filesystems using advanced profiling; and scale storage infrastructure across thousands of nodes.
  • Optimize end-to-end data paths through advanced benchmarking and profiling, contributing high-impact code to open-source storage projects and internal tooling.

Requirements

  • 8+ years in storage engineering, managing distributed storage at multi-petabyte scale
  • Proven track record deploying and operating high-performance storage for GPU/HPC clusters
  • Deep Kubernetes and cloud-native storage experience in production environments
  • Strong coding skills in Go and Python with demonstrated ability to build production-grade systems and tooling
  • BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
  • History of technical leadership: designing systems that significantly improved performance, reliability (99.999%+ uptime), or cost efficiency
  • Distributed Storage Systems: Deep expertise in either of Ceph, WekaFS, Lustre, Vast, GPFS, or similar parallel filesystems at multi-petabyte scale
  • Object Storage: Production experience with S3, MinIO, Ceph, or R2 including performance optimization and cost management
  • Kubernetes Storage: CSI drivers, StatefulSets, PersistentVolumes, storage operators, and custom controllers
  • Storage optimization for GPU workloads, RDMA/InfiniBand networking, parallel filesystem optimization (TB/s aggregate cluster throughput - line saturation)
  • Programming: Go and Python for automation, operators, and tooling
  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, Ansible, Helm, GitOps (ArgoCD)
  • Linux Storage Stack: Advanced knowledge of filesystems (ext4, xfs), LVM, NVMe optimization, RAID configurations
  • Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Thanos architecture and operations

Nice to have 

  • GPU Direct Storage (GDS), NVMe-oF, storage networking, RDMA

jobs.description:
About the Role

Together AI runs one of the largest GPU fleets in the world. The Infra Agent Systems team builds the software systems that power and automate that infrastructure.

We develop production AI agents that diagnose hardware failures, investigate incidents, correlate signals across the fleet, and automate operational workflows. Alongside these agents, we build the platform they run on, including knowledge graphs, retrieval systems, orchestration frameworks, and developer tooling.

You’ll work across two areas:

Infrastructure Agent Systems — Build production AI agents that help operate our GPU fleet by diagnosing failures, investigating incidents, gathering evidence from live systems, and assisting with remediation. These agents are used every day by our infrastructure and datacenter teams through APIs, CLI, dashboards, and Slack.

Core Agent Platform — Build the platform that powers these agents, including knowledge graphs, search and retrieval, orchestration, evaluation, and the tooling that enables agents to reason, act, and continuously improve.

We’re working on something that hasn’t really been done before: building knowledge graphs and self-improving AI agents that understand, operate, and continuously improve large-scale AI infrastructure.

This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of AI agents, distributed systems, infrastructure, and automation, solving challenging engineering problems with real production impact. There’s an enormous amount to build, learn, and shape as we define the future of autonomous infrastructure.

Job Description:
Sharecare is a digital healthcare company that delivers software and tech-enabled services to stakeholders across the healthcare ecosystem to help improve care quality, drive better outcomes, and lower costs. Through its data-driven AI insights, evidence-based resources, and comprehensive platform, including benefits navigation, care management, home care resources, and health information management, Sharecare helps people easily and efficiently manage their healthcare and improve their well-being. Across its three business channels, Sharecare enables health plan sponsors, health systems and physician practices, and leading pharmaceutical brands to drive personalized and value-based care at scale. AskMD by Sharecare, the company’s free AI health app (https://askmd.sharecare.com/) , helps people describe a symptom, ask a health question, and get evidence-based guidance and a clear next step. AskMD is available in the U.S. on the App Store (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/askmd-smart-health-guidance/id739298964) , Google Play (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sharecare.askmd) , and the web (https://askmd.sharecare.com/) . To learn more, visit sharecare.com.
Job Summary:
As the AI Engineer, you will play a critical role across vision, strategy, operations, and execution for defining and driving the transformation of Sharecare into the era of agentic engineering.
We are looking for engineers who can take a big problem domain we hand to them, disappear into it, and they come back with it working, documented, and theirs. We don’t need to check their work or meddle, because checking isn’t unnecessary. The people who have struggled here waited for scoped tickets to tell them what to do, but that’s what we have agents for.
What "a fit" looks like, concretely:
• Demonstrate you can ship daily at high volume with a fleet of AI agents. In the interview we'll ask to see your actual setup and what you let it do unsupervised. "I use Copilot sometimes" is not this.

• You’ve owned architecture across multiple companies or many codebases: staff-plus IC, chief-architect, or platform-consulting background. You've seen a dozen ways teams ship and you have opinions with scars behind them.

• When handed an ambiguous, ugly, load-bearing problem, your instinct is to take it whole: read everything, decide, build, write the doc, tell us what you decided. Not to schedule a meeting about scope.

• Prior experience working in healthcare and/or clinical research, on health data products including electronic health records, claims, wearables, etc. and/or remote patient monitoring technologies is a plus

• You communicate proactively in writing. For example: a Sunday text that says "took care of it, here's the PR and what I changed."

• 6+ years and multiple systems owned end to end

What you will own:
• The Factory spine. Develop and improve our existing factory to maximize and align in the era of agentic engineering. Increase our throughput by 50% while maintaining a lean team. Your job is to evolve our factory platform: Merge gates, migration safety, canary and rollback on a system where a bad deploy can touch patient care.

• The application work spine. The layer that lets AI agents and humans act on patient care with auditability and fail-closed checks. You’ll own the guardrails that ensure agents can safely provide broader components of care.

• The data and metrics. Warehouse, analytics platform, and the pipelines that tell us what happened.

• Architecture syncs with me. You'll have the standing I give someone who has seen more systems than I have: disagree with me, make the call in your domain, unpack it for the team when asked.

Essential Job Functions:
• Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain AI and machine learning solutions to support business needs.

• Build and optimize machine learning models, predictive analytics solutions, recommendation systems, and intelligent automation tool

Data Engineer
The Opportunity:

We are seeking a highly skilled Data Engineer to join our Data team and enable reliable, governed, and high-performing data products on the Army enterprise data platforms. This role plays a crucial part in improving decision-making, readiness visibility, and reporting across Army missions by focusing on data ingestion, transformation, cleaning, quality checks, lineage, and production operations of data while maintaining compliance with platform governance and DoD security requirements.

As the Data Engineer, you will build and operate data pipelines for structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data sources. You'll be cleaning and preparing raw data to ensure accuracy and consistency, followed by applying transformations such as normalization, joins, and incremental loads to create reliable and optimized datasets for downstream analytics and reporting.

The role also requires implementing robust systems for data-quality checks, lineage capture, and monitoring, while troubleshooting pipeline failures through root-cause analysis. You will create and maintain incident response runbooks and optimize routine operations. The position will also involve analyzing and adhering to governance practices, such as permissions management, encryption protocols, and audit logging, ensuring compliance with DoD policies and standards.

Collaboration will be essential, as you will translate mission requirements into technical solutions, develop design documentation for platform adoption, and partner with stakeholders to uphold data quality and governance standards. Using Army data tools, including Pipeline Builder, Code Repositories, Workshop, Slate, and Machinery, you'll deliver robust, scalable data products that drive Army readiness and success.

Join us. The world can't wait.

jobs.title: AI Optimization Engineer
jobs.description:
Position: AI Optimization Engineer
Location: Jersey City, NJ (Hybrid)
Employment type: Contract position
End-customer domain: Bank

We are seeking an experienced AI Optimization Engineer to support large-scale AI/ML and Generative AI workloads for an enterprise environment. This role focuses on optimizing, deploying, and managing machine learning and large language models (LLMs) on GPU-accelerated HPC infrastructure. The ideal candidate will have strong experience in Python-based machine learning, deep learning frameworks, model optimization techniques, and scalable AI infrastructure.

The engineer will work closely with AI, infrastructure, and DevOps teams to design efficient model training and inference pipelines, implement SLURM-based workload orchestration, and deploy containerized ML solutions in production environments. Responsibilities include optimizing model performance using techniques such as pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation, managing inference workflows using Triton Inference Server, and monitoring system performance using Prometheus and Grafana.

This role requires hands-on experience with HPC environments, GPU clusters, containerization technologies, and Linux system administration, along with strong knowledge of machine learning algorithms, deep learning architectures, and modern AI development tools. Experience with cloud platforms, vector embedding, and enterprise-scale AI deployments is highly preferred.
Core Responsibilities:
• Design and optimize AI/ML workloads on GPU-based HPC clusters.
• Deploy and manage large language models (LLMs) in scalable production environments.
• Implement model optimization techniques including pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation.
• Develop and manage automated job scheduling using SLURM with REST and Flask APIs.
• Deploy ML models using containerized microservices architectures.
• Monitor system performance using Prometheus and Grafana.
• Optimize inference pipelines using Triton Inference Server and TRTLLM.
• Conduct exploratory data analysis and model performance evaluation.
• Collaborate with infrastructure and ML teams to improve scalability and efficiency.

The AI Optimization Engineer must have strong experience in Python-based machine learning and deep learning, including NumPy, scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and Keras, with hands-on knowledge of supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, transformer-based models, NLP, CNNs, and Generative AI concepts. The role requires expertise in AI infrastructure and optimization, including HPC environments, GPU clusters, SLURM workload management, Triton Inference Server, TRTLLM, and model optimization techniques such as pruning, quantization, and distillation for scalable LLM deployment.

Candidates should also have experience with DevOps and deployment tools such as Docker, Kubernetes, MLflow, Terraform, Jenkins, GitHub, and Hugging Face, along with strong skills in performance monitoring using Prometheus and Grafana. Additional requirements include Flask API development, Linux administration (RHEL/CentOS), container runtimes like Enroot, Pyxis, and Podman, and experience with data analysis and visualization tools such as Plotly, Seaborn, and Matplotlib.

jobs.description:
About The Role

Cogniify is hiring an AI Data Scientist to build machine learning and NLP models that make our products more relevant and more personal for the people who use them.
You will work hands-on with very large data sets, build and test predictive and recommender models, and run live experiments to check whether your work made a real difference. You will sit close to product managers, software engineers, and designers, so it helps if you enjoy talking through an idea and turning it into a small working version quickly.

This is a remote role based in the United States, with working hours that overlap with Pacific Time preferred.
Core skills for this role: Python, SQL, Hive, SparkSQL, scikit-learn, machine learning, statistical modeling, NLP, recommender systems, feature engineering, and A/B testing.

What You Will Do

• Work hands-on with very large data sets, from initial exploration through to the finished production model.
• Use data mining, NLP, and both supervised and unsupervised machine learning to design, improve, and measure relevance and personalization across the customer journey.
• Work side by side with product managers, software engineers, and designers to plan experiments and build early versions of new ideas.
• Find the data you need, get access, bring it in, clean it up, and make it ready for modeling, including handling your own ETL in SQL, Hive, and SparkSQL.
• Build and improve features from raw data, combining domain knowledge with sound statistics so the model gets better with every round.
• Run A/B tests on a regular basis, collect the results, do the statistical analysis, and explain what your changes did to your peers and to leaders.
• Keep watching new design and technology trends in machine learning and AI, and work out how they could improve what customers get from us.

What We Are Looking For

• A BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Math, Operations Research, Data Science, or a similar technical field.
• At least 4 years of industry experience in data science and applied machine learning.
• At least 4 years of experience with modern analytics tools and programming languages, mainly Python (scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy) along with modern deep learning or NLP libraries.
• Strong skills in SQL, Hive, and SparkSQL for working with large-scale data.
• At least 4 years of applied machine learning and statistical modeling experience—such as classification, regression, decision trees, neural networks, recommender systems, sequential pattern discovery, and text mining—along with hands-on experience in deep learning and embedding-based representations for NLP, language understanding, recommendation, and personalization.
• Clear, grounded communication skills so you can explain complex technical topics to people who are technical and people who are not.

At Danaher, our work saves lives. And each of us plays a part. Fueled by our culture of continuous improvement, we turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.

Our 60,000+ associates work across the globe at more than 15 unique businesses within life sciences, diagnostics, and biotechnology.

Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference? At Danaher, you can build an incredible career at a leading science and technology company, where we’re committed to hiring and developing from within. Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.

The Senior MLOps Engineer is responsible for owning significant parts of the machine learning and agentic AI lifecycle that powers Danaher’s next generation of AI-driven products and automations. You will take models and AI agents from experimentation to reliable, scalable production. In this high-impact role, you will design and operate the pipelines, serving infrastructure, orchestration, and observability that let data scientists, engineers, and business teams build and run ML models and agentic workflows with speed, reproducibility, and rigor. You will partner with teams across Danaher’s operating companies to turn promising AI prototypes into governed, production-grade agentic automations that run efficiently at scale on shared compute.

This position reports to the Senior Director, Data and AI Platform and is part of the Chief Information Officer (CIO) Office located in Washington, DC and will be fully remote.

The Annapurna Labs team at Amazon Web Services (AWS) builds AWS Neuron, the software development kit used to accelerate deep learning and GenAI workloads on Amazon’s custom machine learning accelerators, Inferentia and Trainium. The AWS Neuron SDK, developed by the Annapurna Labs team at AWS, is the backbone for accelerating deep learning and GenAI workloads on Amazon's Inferentia and Trainium ML accelerators. This comprehensive toolkit includes an ML compiler, runtime, and application framework that seamlessly integrates with popular ML frameworks like PyTorch and JAX enabling unparalleled ML inference and training performance. The Inference Enablement and Acceleration team is at the forefront of running a wide range of models and supporting novel architecture alongside maximizing their performance for AWS's custom ML accelerators. Working across the stack from PyTorch till the hardware-software boundary, our engineers build systematic infrastructure, innovate new methods and create high-performance kernels for ML functions, ensuring every compute unit is fine tuned for optimal performance for our customers' demanding workloads. We combine deep hardware knowledge with ML expertise to push the boundaries of what's possible in AI acceleration. As part of the broader Neuron organization, our team works across multiple technology layers - from frameworks and kernels and collaborate with compiler to runtime and collectives. We not only optimize current performance but also contribute to future architecture designs, working closely with customers to enable their models and ensure optimal performance. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of machine learning, high-performance computing, and distributed architectures, where you'll help shape the future of AI acceleration technology You will architect and implement business critical features, and mentor a brilliant team of experienced engineers. We operate in spaces that are very large, yet our teams remain small and agile. There is no blueprint. We're inventing. We're experimenting. It is a very unique learning culture. The team works closely with customers on their model enablement, providing direct support and optimization expertise to ensure their machine learning workloads achieve optimal performance on AWS ML accelerators. The team collaborates with open source ecosystems to provide seamless integration and bring peak performance at scale for customers and developers. This role is responsible for development, enablement and performance tuning of a wide variety of LLM model families, including massive scale large language models like the Llama family, DeepSeek and beyond. The Inference Enablement and Acceleration team works side by side with compiler engineers and runtime engineers to create, build and tune distributed inference solutions with Trainium and Inferentia. Experience optimizing inference performance for both latency and throughput on such large models across the stack from system level optimizations through to Pytorch or JAX is a must have. jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI Developer Productivity
jobs.description:
Mirage is an AI video company focused on making creation dramatically easier. Our team tackles some of the hardest creative and technical challenges in generative media.
We get to rethink how people collaborate with AI that can actually do creative work with them—defining entirely new interaction paradigms for AI-native video tools. We make that possible by building multimodal agents that turn creative direction into edits, rendering engines that composite multiple layers of video and graphics, and generative video models trained from the ground up that create new media when needed.
All of this comes together in Captions, our creative workspace for generating, editing, and designing video. The technology behind Captions is now available more broadly: Tesseract gives any AI agent native video-editing capabilities, while developers can integrate our models into their own products through APIs.
Explore our work
Captions — Our flagship creative workspace
Tesseract — Our professional video engine for AI agents
Research — The foundation models we build in-house
Updates — The latest from Mirage
TechCrunch, Forbes, Fast Company — Press
Our Investors
We’re very fortunate to have some the best investors and entrepreneurs backing us, including Index Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, Uncommon Projects, Kevin Systrom, Mike Krieger, Lenny Rachitsky, Antoine Martin, Julie Zhuo, Ben Rubin, Jaren Glover, SVAngel, 20VC, Ludlow Ventures, Chapter One, and more.
Please note that most of our roles will require you to be in-person at our NYC HQ (located in Union Square)

About the role
Mirage is hiring a backend engineer to rebuild how we ship software as AI agents dramatically increase the volume of code we produce. You’ll own the path from commit to production, ensuring our build, test, review, deployment, and security systems help engineers and their agents ship quickly and safely.
You’ll treat our development infrastructure like a product—working directly with engineers to understand friction, measure bottlenecks, and build tools they want to use. You’ll also ship features across our AI video products and developer platform, grounding those improvements in firsthand experience.
While we don’t use hierarchical titles or levels internally, we are currently hiring engineers who have operated at senior or staff+ scope.
Responsibilities
• Ship features alongside product engineers across our video creation software, video rendering engine, and developer platform, identifying where our development systems slow them down

• Turn those insights into tools, agents, and streamlined workflows that engineers choose because they’re the fastest way to ship

• Rebuild CI/CD to support 100x the change volume through fast incremental builds, test selection, automated flaky-test detection and quarantine, merge queues, and preview environments

• Make deployments safe by default through progressive rollouts, automated canary analysis, feature flags, and automatic rollback, catching bad changes within minutes before they affect users

• Own the environments coding agents work in, including sandboxes, ephemeral stacks, and the tooling agents need to build, test, and verify their own work

• Build an AI review pipeline with agent reviewers tuned to our codebase, risk-based routing that directs risky changes to humans, and automated policy checks that gate merges

• Run continuous, agent-driven penetration testing against our applications, APIs, and infrastructure, moving beyond point-in-time annual audits and turning findings into pull requests with proposed fixes

• Integrate security into the development pipeline through secrets, dependency, and supply-chain scanning, AI-assisted vulnerability triage, and automatically generated fix PRs

• Secure agents’ access to code, infrastructure, and data through least-privilege permissions, short-lived credentials, sandboxing, audit logs, and prompt-injection guardrails

About the role

At Rippling, we are not just building AI features, we are building an autonomous operating system for work. We are investing heavily in the next generation of enterprise AI: intelligent background automation, systems that monitor and improve themselves, and a custom intelligence layer built on Rippling's unique data and workflows.

The opportunity is to push the boundaries of what machine learning can do in the enterprise through purpose-built ML systems that learn from Rippling's proprietary data graph to deliver compounding intelligence across every product surface. You will be joining the team that recently launched Rippling AI, the fastest-growing product in Rippling's history. The models and ML systems you build will be the intelligence powering every AI surface at Rippling.

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, you will own the end-to-end ML lifecycle for projects within the AI Cloud team: problem formulation, data preparation, model development, evaluation, and production deployment. • Contribute to design and code reviews, share ML best practices, and mentor engineers within the team.

• Strong practical experience with modern ML, including LLMs, transformer architectures, fine-tuning, and RAG; familiarity with RLHF or related model-alignment techniques.
• Strong fundamentals in classical ML and statistics.
