jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.description:
About the position

The Data Scientist in Process Development supports data integration and expands data visualization and modeling capabilities for biotherapeutics process development. The role transforms complex process data into clear insights that support scientific research, development, testing, and process improvement. It analyzes data from materials, processes, and experiments under a range of conditions to support better decisions across development work.

The position works independently on complex data analysis, selects appropriate methods, and communicates findings to scientific and technical audiences. It may serve as a technical resource and trainer for team members, contribute to process improvements, and participate in external collaborations and knowledge transfer.

Responsibilities
• Develop, implement, and support data integration workflows that combine process development data from multiple sources.
• Build and improve data visualizations and dashboards to help teams explore trends, patterns, and process performance.
• Develop statistical and predictive models to support biotherapeutics process development and data-driven decision-making.
• Analyze complex datasets independently and identify insights, anomalies, and opportunities for improvement.
• Work with scientific and technical teams to define data needs, align on analysis approaches, and support project timelines and deliverables.
• Present data findings, models, and technical updates at team meetings and project reviews.
• Troubleshoot data, software, or analysis issues and recommend practical improvements.
• Serve as a technical resource and trainer for the team on data tools, analysis methods, and visualization practices.
• Participate in external collaborations and interactions to support data analysis, model development, and knowledge transfer.
• Support junior team members and contribute to process improvements through data-driven insights.

Requirements
• Bachelor’s degree with 8 or more years of experience, Master’s degree with 6 or more years of experience, or PhD in data sciences or a related field.
• Experience as a data scientist, data analyst, or in a similar role supporting scientific or process development work.
• Strong experience with data integration, data cleaning, and working across multiple data sources.
• Strong experience building data visualizations, dashboards, and reports for technical audiences.
• Experience developing statistical, machine learning, or predictive models for scientific or process data.
• Understanding of biotherapeutics process development, biopharmaceutical data, or related laboratory and manufacturing data.
• Ability to analyze complex data independently, select appropriate methods, and communicate findings clearly.
• Familiarity with laboratory, process development, or manufacturing systems used to generate and manage scientific data.
• Ability to support junior team members and contribute to process improvements through data-driven insights.

jobs.title: AI Data Scientist - USA
jobs.description:
About The Role

Cogniify is hiring an AI Data Scientist to build machine learning and NLP models that make our products more relevant and more personal for the people who use them.
You will work hands-on with very large data sets, build and test predictive and recommender models, and run live experiments to check whether your work made a real difference. You will sit close to product managers, software engineers, and designers, so it helps if you enjoy talking through an idea and turning it into a small working version quickly.

This is a remote role based in the United States, with working hours that overlap with Pacific Time preferred.
Core skills for this role: Python, SQL, Hive, SparkSQL, scikit-learn, machine learning, statistical modeling, NLP, recommender systems, feature engineering, and A/B testing.

What You Will Do

• Work hands-on with very large data sets, from initial exploration through to the finished production model.
• Use data mining, NLP, and both supervised and unsupervised machine learning to design, improve, and measure relevance and personalization across the customer journey.
• Work side by side with product managers, software engineers, and designers to plan experiments and build early versions of new ideas.
• Find the data you need, get access, bring it in, clean it up, and make it ready for modeling, including handling your own ETL in SQL, Hive, and SparkSQL.
• Build and improve features from raw data, combining domain knowledge with sound statistics so the model gets better with every round.
• Run A/B tests on a regular basis, collect the results, do the statistical analysis, and explain what your changes did to your peers and to leaders.
• Keep watching new design and technology trends in machine learning and AI, and work out how they could improve what customers get from us.

What We Are Looking For

• A BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Math, Operations Research, Data Science, or a similar technical field.
• At least 4 years of industry experience in data science and applied machine learning.
• At least 4 years of experience with modern analytics tools and programming languages, mainly Python (scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy) along with modern deep learning or NLP libraries.
• Strong skills in SQL, Hive, and SparkSQL for working with large-scale data.
• At least 4 years of applied machine learning and statistical modeling experience—such as classification, regression, decision trees, neural networks, recommender systems, sequential pattern discovery, and text mining—along with hands-on experience in deep learning and embedding-based representations for NLP, language understanding, recommendation, and personalization.
• Clear, grounded communication skills so you can explain complex technical topics to people who are technical and people who are not.

Perks and Benefits of Working With Us

• Unlimited PTO
• Generous parental leave, well above industry standards
• Medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees
• Disability and life insurance
• Mental health and wellbeing support
• Annual bonus program
• Employer Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)
• Yearly team-building experiences
• Mentorship and sponsorship opportunities
• Manager resources and support
• Small teams where your work makes a real difference
• Open communication with management and company leadership
• An entrepreneurial culture where taking initiative is part of everyday work

Cogniify is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - AI Compute, Together Cloud
jobs.description:
About the Role

Together AI is building the AI Native Cloud, an end-to-end platform for the full generative AI lifecycle, combining the fastest LLM inference engine with state-of-the-art GPU cloud infrastructure. The Together Cloud team builds the [Together GPU Clusters](https://www.together.ai/gpu-clusters) flagship IaaS product that provides high-performance, AI-ready GPU clusters through a self-serve cloud console, along with the virtualized infrastructure layer powering Together's inference, RL, and fine-tuning products.

As a Senior Software Engineer focusing on AI Compute in the Together Cloud org, you will build and own major components of the next generation AI cloud platform – a highly available, global cloud infrastructure with cutting-edge virtualization of the latest ML hardware: GB300s/VRs, BlueField DPUs, InfiniBand and dual/quad-plane RoCEv2 fabrics. That virtualized computing platform powers our own SaaS products – inference, RL, and fine-tuning – and serves external cloud customers through self-serve offerings such as on-demand/reserved Kubernetes/Slurm clusters, across dozens of data centers and hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

The hard problems in rapidly scaling heterogeneous GPU fleets are software problems: fully automated bootstrapping of GPU data centers, high-performance virtualization of GPU compute and DC networking without compromising isolation or portability, and fault-tolerant decentralized control planes. We solve them by building global and in-DC services, Kubernetes operators, and high-performance SDN libraries, forking hypervisors and Linux kernels, and building infra tailored to inference and fine-tuning. You'll own massive greenfield projects across their full lifecycle – scoping the problem and writing PRDs with our PMs, designing the system, and building it through to GA launch.

Responsibilities

  • Build the GPU and network virtualization stack: the hypervisor, kernel, and SDN work that makes GPU compute and DC networking high-performance, portable, and strongly isolated across heterogeneous hardware.
  • Build and maintain our in-DC IaaS layer: the services, Kubernetes operators, and libraries that provision and manage compute, storage, and networks in our data centers, including VMs, parallel filesystems, VPCs, and InfiniBand partitions. Implement and harden the bring-up path for a new Vera Rubin data center with thousands of GPUs.
  • Scale the distributed GPU scheduling and global management plane: the control-plane services behind on-demand and reserved clusters, including the automation that onboards new capacity and raises per-cluster limits.
  • Harden the monitoring and automated remediation layer for fault tolerance: automated detection, isolation, and recovery of failed nodes that keeps distributed pretraining and large-scale inference fault-tolerant.
  • Own your components end-to-end: write the design docs, break the work into milestones that ship incrementally, and improve the reliability of what's already in production.
  • Raise the bar around you: code review, design feedback, and mentoring junior engineers.
  • Build the tooling other teams rely on: testing frameworks, developer tools, and documentation that make our systems robust and usable across teams, plus contributions to the core, open-source Together AI platform.

To be successful, you'll need to be deeply technical, ready to own projects truly end-to-end, and an excellent communicator — strong software development fundamentals, strong systems knowledge and troubleshooting instincts, and the collaboration and diplomacy skills to work across teams.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional software development experience, with strong proficiency in at least one ba

jobs.description:
About the Role

We're looking for a Software Engineer to build the systems that treat infrastructure as software. This role owns the software state machines that provision hardware, bring it into service, and manage its full lifecycle — turning racks of GPUs into running inference clusters without a human touching a runbook. The Research and Inference team is your customer: today they file tickets and wait; the target state is that they issue a single API call to stand up, scale, or tear down a cluster, and the system takes care of the rest. The platform is manifest-driven such that teams declare the desired state of a cluster or host — shape, topology, software stack — and the system is responsible for reconciling reality to that manifest, continuously, through every stage of its lifecycle. You will design the engines that manifest the schema, the engines that execute against it, and the workflows that carry a piece of hardware or a cluster from one state to the next—taking it from bare metal to a fully functioning AI cluster for training or inference.

You'll write production code which is typed, tested, versioned, and deployed through CI/CD that models infrastructure state and reconciles it, the same way a Kubernetes controller reconciles a cluster's desired state. Success looks like eliminating manual provisioning work, not documenting it better.

 - Customer centricity and ownership mentality

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. 

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Strategic Finance Data Science helps OpenAI make consequential financial and operating decisions as the business grows. We connect customer behavior, product economics and business performance to the choices leaders make about goals, customer acquisition and investment.

We are seeking a data science leader who can turn complex, uncertain business questions into clear recommendations. You will lead an established team, strengthen its technical and leadership capabilities, and help shape where it can have the greatest impact.

You will partner with Finance and business leaders on forecasts, customer lifetime value, acquisition economics and resource allocation. This role calls for someone who can challenge assumptions, explain tradeoffs and follow the analysis through to a decision. You should be motivated by the opportunity to build a durable function during a period of rapid growth.

About the Role

We're looking for a software engineer, reliability-minded but still a builder, to own what happens in production to the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. The platform team builds the manifest-driven API and controllers that let the inference team declare what they need, a cluster, a model deployment, a capacity change, and get it reconciled underneath. Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page.

The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. Strong candidates have hands-on production-reliability experience on large-scale distributed or GPU-serving systems, are comfortable troubleshooting InfiniBand/RDMA and Kubernetes controller/CRD-based platforms, and think about GPU infrastructure, and the tools that keep it reliable, as software to be engineered.

jobs.title: Hardware Engineer
jobs.description:
Bedrock Robotics, Inc. seeks a Hardware Engineer in San Francisco, CA responsible for designing, manufacturing, and testing its autonomous hardware systems, including high performance computer systems, sensors, controllers, interfaces to machines, and testing equipment.

This position will work with autonomous hardware systems installed on standard heavy construction machinery—excavators, bulldozers, and wheel loaders—to allow that equipment to perform earthmoving work on construction sites autonomously. In this context, “autonomous hardware systems” are the physical electronic components installed on a construction machine that allow it to operate without a human operator in the cab. They consist of: high-performance computer systems (ruggedized onboard computers mounted on the machine that perform the calculations required for autonomous operation); sensors (devices that allow the machine to perceive its surroundings, including cameras, radar, lidar, and GNSS); controllers and interfaces (electronic units that translate the computer's decisions into electrical signals that operate the machine's existing hydraulic, steering, and engine controls); and testing equipment (benches, fixtures, and instrumentation used to verify each of the above components before and after installation on a machine). Working together, these systems continuously collect sensor data, determine the machine's position and what is around it, calculate the path the machine should follow and the movements it should make, and then command the machine's controls to carry out those movements, performing the tasks a human operator would otherwise perform manually.

Specific duties include: (i) defining and designing hardware systems, including component-level architecture for autonomous machines and camera/optics design and performance; (ii) establishing and leading relationships and programs with external vendors to facilitate hardware manufacturing and delivery; (iii) supporting hardware system verification and validation, including working with safety teams to establish/tune requirements and performance metrics for components and systems; (iv) using industry standard tools and knowledge to test standards of hardware systems; and (v) writing reusable, high quality sensor data analysis and testing automation software.

This is a hybrid office-based/work-from-home position within the United States. The employee can work remotely from within the United States but must be able to work in the San Francisco office at least three (3) days per week.

Must have a bachelor’s degree (or foreign equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Robotics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a directly related field plus five (5) years of progressively responsible, post-baccalaureate experience in designing, integrating, and validating electrical hardware systems.

Must have any experience with: (i) high performance computer systems, including x86 or ARM; (ii) robotics sensors stacks, including lidar, radar, camera, or GNSS; (iii) communication protocols and technologies, including CAN, LIN, J1939, FlexRay, or Ethernet; (iv) python or C++/C/Rust; and (v) standardization tools and organizations, including ISO, SAE, and ANSI.

Must be willing and able to travel regionally/nationally up to 15%, to visit hardware testing sites.

Experience can be concurrent.

This position is expected to pay an annual salary of $236,000.

Apply online at bedrockrobotics.com/careers http://bedrockrobotics.com/careers.

jobs.title: [Junior / Senior / Staff] Software Engineer, Inference / Compute Infrastructure Engineering
jobs.description:
About the Role

We're looking for a software engineer to build the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. You'll design a manifest-driven API where the inference team declares what they need, whether that's a cluster, a model deployment, or a capacity change, and our controllers handle the reconciliation, provider/runtime selection, and lifecycle management underneath, so the inference team never has to know or care which specific serving stack, scheduler, or hardware pool is doing the work. You'll also build the systems that keep the fleet efficient, not just running, including defragmentation and rebalancing logic that consolidates scattered workloads back into contiguous capacity, and scheduling/bin-packing improvements that push GPU utilization up without hurting latency.

The core value we're after is decoupling the people building on top of the platform from the operational and runtime complexity underneath, while squeezing more usable capacity out of the same hardware. You'll build the controllers, reconciliation loops, and self-service surface (API/CLI, not tickets) that make that decoupling real, plus the event-driven health, remediation, and utilization systems that keep it running and efficient without a human in the loop. Strong candidates have hands-on experience with Kubernetes controller/CRD patterns, have built or operated a platform API that abstracts multiple backends behind one interface, understand GPU scheduling and capacity efficiency (fragmentation, bin-packing, right-sizing), and think about GPU infrastructure as software to be engineered.

A product mindset - you've built internal platforms or APIs consumed by other engineering teams and care about the developer experience of what you ship.You build it, you own it. You are not only responsible for delivering the software but also for operating and supporting it in production.

Responsibilities

  • Build the provisioning state machine: design and implement the software that models the full lifecycle of a physical host from discovery, inference bring-up to GPU driver/CUDA stack, health validation, and decommission/RMA — as explicit, versioned states and transitions.
  • Build the self-service API: design declarative APIs and a control plane so the inference team can request, scale, and tear down inference clusters with one API call — no ticket, no human in the loop.
  • Automate self-healing: detect degraded or failed nodes, drain them safely, trigger repair or replacement, and reintroduce healthy capacity into the pool automatically.
  • Own reliability of the pipeline: idempotency, retries, rollback, and drift detection so the provisioning system is as dependable as any other production service.
  • Partner with the inference/ML platform team: understand the cluster shapes they need — topology, interconnect, scheduling constraints — and encode them as first-class abstractions in the platform.
  • Engineer it like software: strong typing, automated tests, code review, versioning, and CI/CD for infrastructure code — this is a product, not a collection of Ansible playbooks.

Requirements

Core requirements (all levels):

  • Strong software engineering background in Go, Python, Rust, or similar — you write and test real software for a living.
  • Experience with durable workflow orchestration tools such as Temporal, Cadence, or equivalent to run long-lived, manifest-driven workflows that survive failures and resume mid-execution.
  • Experience building software control planes or orchestration systems that model state and reconcile it over time (e.g., Kubernetes controllers/operators, custom reconciliation loops, workflow engines).

jobs.description: University of Cambridge, University of Manchester | PhD in AI / Earth Observation / Environmental Science | ONSITE | UK home fee status only | £30k tax-free annual stipend Our group at Cambridge works on Earth Observation foundation models (Tessera: v1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20380 , v2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03949 , https://geotessera.org/ ) and we've started a collaboration with Manchester to understand how they can be used to improve pollution models and then environmental decision making in general. jobs.title: Full-Stack Engineer (Backend Leaning) - Studio
jobs.description:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
Studio is where creators build and finish video on ElevenLabs, powered by our generative graph engine, Flows. You’ll own our “produce once, distribute everywhere” workflow. It takes a finished Studio project and runs it through our dubbing pipeline to produce it in many languages and aspect ratios, with auto-translated captions. Today that means duplicating and rebuilding projects by hand.
This work is entirely greenfield: the specs aren’t written yet. You’ll shape them through written proposals (RFCs), pressure-test data structures with the team lead, and carry the project from first draft to launch.
You’re a strong backend generalist who is good with complex data structures and has the product instincts to decide what’s worth building.


Requirements

 - Strong backend generalist who has designed and shipped complex, data-heavy systems end to end.

 - Comfortable with enterprise-grade concerns such as usage reporting and accounts.

 - Evidence of product ownership: side projects, open source, or work in a product-facing context.

 - Has taken projects from inception to launch with little hand-holding.

Bonus: experience with media or video-processing pipelines (helpful, not required)

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender

jobs.description:
Dataiku is the Platform for AI Success, the enterprise orchestration layer for building, deploying, and governing AI. In a single environment, teams design and operate analytics, machine learning, and AI agents with the transparency, collaboration, and control enterprises require. Sitting above data platforms, cloud infrastructure, and AI services, Dataiku connects the full enterprise AI stack - empowering organizations to run AI across multi-vendor environments with centralized governance.

The world’s leading companies rely on Dataiku to operationalize AI and run it as a true business performance engine delivering measurable value. For more, visit the Dataiku blog, LinkedIn, X, and YouTube.

The world's biggest companies come to dataiku.com to figure out how to make AI work for them. Your job is to make that experience fast, sharp, and built to convert. You’ll own the code behind dataiku.com: every component, A/B test, and tracking tag that ships goes through you.

You'll be embedded in the marketing organization: reporting to the Head of Web, part of Growth, Demand Generation & Digital Marketing, and working every day with our Web team and Designers. You'll team up with the rest of the Growth teams to find what converts. With IT and R&D, you'll ship code that meets the same standards as our product.

What you'll work on:

Build

  • Product launches, events for 1,000+ attendees, interactive experiences, and campaign pages: you will own all the development of all the marketing web experiences. You'll take them from Figma to production with the web team, marketers, and design.
  • Own the Contentful content model and component library: content types, validations, references, and reusable sections. Design system first, always, so marketers can build pages without breaking design, forms, tracking, or SEO.
  • Ship code that's QAd and ready. You'll check it across devices, browsers, and tracking before anyone else has to.

Optimize

  • Make pages fast and keep them fast. Core Web Vitals are your scoreboard.
  • Build A/B tests and personalized experiences with Growth and Paid. Read the results, ship the winner, run the next one.
  • Keep the technical SEO and AEO tight: structured data, redirects, hreflang, crawlability, and the files and markup that help AI systems read the site.

Measure

  • Own tracking in Google Tag Manager across organic and paid, including taking over day-to-day tag maintenance from our external provider: the data layer, GA4 events, pixels, conversion APIs, and consent mode.
  • Spot the broken funnel or the attribution gap before anyone asks, and come up with the fix.

Automate

  • Build AI agents into the release process: code-reviews, first-pass QA, accessibility checks, and link and metadata audits, so people spend review time on judgment calls.
  • Work with marketers and the growth team to embed them into agentic processes.

You are a good fit if:

  • You've spent at least 4+ years in web development, ideally on marketing sites, at an agency, or on a growth team.
  • You have hands-on experience managing a website in Contentful.
  • You're strong in React, JavaScript/TypeScr

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
We build an ads engine that learns as it goes: brand book, taste, and what actually performs in every market. It plans, generates, localizes, launches and learns from ads across the major ad platforms, using ElevenLabs’ full audio and video stack.
You’ll be a founding engineer for a product area of your own. There’s no PM and no handed-down spec. You’ll talk to users, decide what to build, and ship it across the stack, from data pipelines and agent tools to the UI. Early work could include feeding competitive intelligence into the engine’s weekly briefs or launching a new ad format.
We’re looking for founders and founding engineers. You’d rather ship a rough v0 on Friday than a perfect design doc. Strong engineering is the minimum. What sets people apart is product judgment and ownership.

Requirements

 - Has built and shipped a product end-to-end without anyone handing them a spec, ideally as a founder or one of the first engineers.

 - Strong full-stack product engineer (frontend- or backend-leaning is fine) who can build a pipeline, an agent tool and the UI

 - Builds with LLMs and agents pragmatically: tools, retrieval and evals, not model research.

 - Talks to users without being asked, and can say what they’d build first and why.

Bonus: experience with ad platforms, adtech or marketing tools;

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, AI Delivery (Dammam)
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We’re seeking an experienced Engineering Program Manager to join Cohere’s customer-facing Engineering Program Management team. We need someone with curiosity, drive, independence, and leadership, who has hands-on experience working directly with customers and managing projects for enterprise-grade software or enterprise-focused machine learning solutions. In return, you’ll have the unique opportunity to shape Cohere’s operations, collaborate with leading minds in the LLM space, work directly with our Strategic Customers as well as Applied ML (AML) Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Platform , Product and Go-to-Market teams, and be the “technical” voice of Cohere for the customer. You will get a chance to create extremely high-impact contributions to our fast-growing company, product and culture.

Please Note: This role is open to candidates based in [Dammam]

As an Engineering Program Manager/ Technical Program Manager, you will:

 - Communicate: Provide clear, timely, and objective communication across the tech organization, Cohere teams, leadership, and most importantly - our strategic customers and external partners.

 - Optimize: Break down complex issues into strategies, driving engineering alignment with product, business, and marketing while fostering collaboration.

 - Plan: Create and manage program/project schedules, identify dependencies, manage risks, and drive organizational alignment.

 - Execute: Ensure on-time delivery, identify development needs, and establish checkpoints for status updates.

 - Problem solve: Proactively identify and resolve issues, coordinate cross-functional dependencies, and prioritize impacts to schedule and product quality.

You may be a good fit if:

 - You have at least 5 years of experience as an Engineering or Technical Program Manager, with at least 3 years in customer-facing technical delivery and operations focused on enterprise-grade AI software/solutions

 - Knowledge or experience with LLM training or optimization would be a key differentiator

 - You are problem-focused and making customers successful really excites you

 - You are detail-oriented and extremely self-organized. You love enabling people and teams around you, and are excellent at capturing detailed notes/action items during highly technical meetings and tracking progress.

 - You have a Bias for Action - you are very execution focused and you like getting things done.

 - You have experience working with cross-functional teams to get technical products, services or solutions shipped to an internal or an external customer and can independently own tracking and reporting across multiple work-streams, with owners in different time-zones.

 - You are comfortable holding leaders and individual contributors accountable. You can be assertive while remaining diplomatic. You are not afraid to follow up with people to ensure shipping within committed deadlines.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a sepa

jobs.title: AI-Native Product Engineer - Senior
jobs.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

Turn emerging AI capabilities into products people choose to use, trust, and rely on. You will work as an end-to-end builder, close to users, product decisions, and production code, connecting the pieces that turn an AI demonstration into a durable product.

This role suits an engineer with founder-like ownership and the discipline to test assumptions early. You may move from a user conversation to a working prototype, from that prototype to a secure service, and from a production failure to a better evaluation in the same product cycle. Speed matters, but so do accessibility, maintainability, and the willingness to simplify when the evidence calls for it.

About Challenger

Challenger is a new EY program focused on building the firm’s next generation of services. It pursues opportunities where AI enables a fundamentally different service and way of delivering it, including rethinking existing offerings and developing new ones.

Small, dedicated teams build and test ideas in real conditions. Solutions that demonstrate clear business value and operational readiness transition to the business for adoption and scale.

Challenger Core develops and maintains the shared technology, methods, and risk and quality guardrails that support this work. Each team contributes reusable tools and practices, helping make the next service faster and less costly to build.

Your Key Responsibilities

• Start with the user. Work directly with users and domain experts to understand real workflows, observe friction, and identify where AI can create distinctive value.
• Test assumptions quickly. Turn product hypotheses into concise specifications, prototypes, and small releases that generate useful evidence early.
• Own complete product slices. Build coherent verticals across the experience, services, data, AI behavior, and enterprise integrations rather than optimizing a single layer.
• Shape AI behavior. Design instructions, context, retrieval, structured outputs, and tool use, choosing adaptation or tuning only when evidence supports it.
• Build the evidence system. Create representative tasks and automated evaluations that show whether the product is useful, correct, safe, accessible, and improving.
• Connect outcomes to behavior. Instrument user journeys so the team can relate adoption and task success to system behavior, latency, failures, and cost.
• Engineer for responsible use. Build clear permission boundaries, secure data handling, human checkpoints, graceful degradation, recovery, and rollback into the experience.
• Own production quality. Release incrementally, monitor live behavior, respond to incidents, and turn failures into durable product and engineering improvements.
• Make practical trade-offs. Balance experience, quality, speed, reliability, and cost, using deterministic software when it is the more dependable choice.
• Contribute reusable patterns. Share proven components and evaluation assets with the broader platform while remaining accountable for their performance in the product workflow.

Skills And Attributes For Success

• Full-stack engineering: Strong ability to build maintainable production software across modern interfaces, services, APIs, data, and integrations.
• AI application depth: Practical knowledge of model APIs, context design, retrieval, tool use, structured outputs, and agentic patterns.
• Product judgment: Ability to find the real user problem, frame clear hypotheses, and simplify the solution when evidence challenges the original idea.
• Evaluation discipline: Experience designing representative tests and experiments for systems whose behavior is not fully deterministic.
• Production ownership: Strong instincts for observability,

jobs.title: AI Systems Engineer - DevOps& Observability Manager
jobs.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

We are seeking an AI Systems Engineer to own the delivery, model-serving, routing, and observability layer of EY’s AI-native platform. These are the systems that ship, run, and make fully visible every AI workload. Within the Hybrid AI Multi-Environment Runtime (HAI), this role owns how AI services and agents are built and deployed, how models execute, how requests are routed to them, how AI assets are catalogued and governed, how consumption is measured and bounded, and how the entire platform is observed across cloud, on-prem, edge, and air-gapped environments.

This is a distinct discipline from platform, data, and trust engineering. Where Platform Engineering owns the cluster substrate and its infrastructure automation, this role owns the delivery and runtime surface, including the CI/CD/CV pipelines that ship AI workloads, secure model execution, semantic routing, and model/prompt selection, together with the governance, discovery, cost, and telemetry systems that keep AI workloads shippable, economical, discoverable, and transparent. It sits at the intersection of DevOps, MLOps, FinOps, and observability.

This role is ideal for an engineer who is equally comfortable building automated delivery pipelines, operating high-performance inference (GPUs, model servers, sandboxed execution), and building deep observability and cost visibility; who understands that in regulated contexts every AI workload must be delivered repeatably and every AI request must be economically bounded, attributable, and traceable end-to-end.

Your Key Responsibilities

• Own DevOps and delivery for AI workloads: build and operate the CI/CD/CV pipelines that ship AI services, agents, and runtime components, including automated build, test, continuous verification, release, and rollback, so AI workloads are delivered repeatably and safely into every environment.
• Own governance and discovery for AI assets, including service catalog/registry (Artifactory/Nexus, Harbor), experiment tracking and model metadata (MLflow), upstream registries/mirrors (HuggingFace/NGC), CVE/SBOM scanning (Trivy), lineage contracts (OpenLineage), and license management.
• Own resource and cost management, including quotas and rate limits, cost attribution and utilization (Apptio/OpenCost/Kubecost), so AI execution stays economically bounded and controllable per tenant and engagement.
• Own the full observability stack, including metrics (Prometheus/Mimir), logs (Loki), traces (Tempo/Jaeger), dashboards (Grafana), LLM debugging and evaluation (LangSmith/Langfuse), and SLA/alert notifications.
• Own the OpenTelemetry collection layer, including multi-tenant receiver, exporters and queues (Kafka sink), DCGM exporter for GPU telemetry, processor batching, and dynamic filtering, so every signal is captured and routed reliably.
• Automate GitOps-based delivery and continuous verification; embedding quality, integrity, and cost gates into pipelines so releases are policy-compliant by default rather than by manual review.
• Close the loop between delivery and observability by using telemetry, evaluation, and cost signals to drive deployment decisions, progressive rollout, and automated rollback of AI workloads.
• Ensure cost and telemetry are identity-stamped and per-tenant, so consumption and behavior are attributable end-to-end, keeping FinOps and observability tied to the workloads that generate the load.

Skills And Attributes For Success

• Strong DevOps expertise: CI/CD/CV pipeline design, GitOps, continuous verification, and progressive/automated release and rollback for production workloads.
• Deep expertise operating model-serving and inference systems (Ray, vLLM/Triton/NIM) on GPUs at production

Teradyne is building dedicated, in-house AI security engineering capability within the Information Security organization to keep pace with the rapid adoption of AI agents, large language models (LLMs), and AI-enabled tooling across the enterprise. As AI becomes embedded in how the company operates, from everyday productivity tools to autonomous agents to security operations itself, Teradyne needs an engineer who can both lock down how AI is used across the enterprise and put AI to work strengthening our own cyber defenses. Software Kubernetes Engineer

This role focuses on Kubernetes-based platform engineering to support Navy programs within a highly secure, air-gapped environment. This is a full time role that offers benefits and PTO. Position is onsite, with a 4/10 work schedule (off every Friday). You will specialize in packaging, integrating, and deploying containerized applications across Kubernetes clusters, working primarily in a Linux ecosystem. Acting as a subject matter expert in containerization, you will collaborate closely with program architects to evaluate tools, onboard solutions, and operationalize Kubernetes deployments.

Responsibilities
• Lead the end-to-end container packaging, build, and deployment processes into Kubernetes environments, with an emphasis on air-gapped systems.
• Evaluate, research, and vet containerization and platform tooling solutions to ensure they meet program and security requirements.
• Partner with architects to integrate microservices and legacy applications into Kubernetes-based platforms.
• Develop and manage Helm charts for packaging, versioning, and deploying applications into Kubernetes clusters.
• Configure and manage deployments using YAML manifests and CI tooling, with a preference for GitLab CI.
• Troubleshoot Kubernetes environments using command-line diagnostics, including pods, clusters, and log analysis.

• Support deployment activities across networked environments, including subnets and VLANs, ensuring reliable connectivity and performance.

• Active Secret clearance.
• Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes, including deployment, integration, and troubleshooting.
• Deep experience with containerization using Docker and/or Podman.
• Proven expertise with RHEL-based Linux systems, including CLI troubleshooting and system diagnostics.
• Experience with Bash and/or Python scripting for automation and tooling.
• Experience working with CI pipelines, with GitLab CI preferred.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Secure Intelligence Institute)
jobs.description:
Perplexity is seeking energetic researchers and engineers to join our Secure Intelligence Institute (SII), Perplexity's flagship research center for advancing security, privacy, and trust in frontier intelligence. SII’s goals are to advance frontier AI security research, translate those advances into concrete improvements in Perplexity's systems, and share knowledge and resources that strengthen the broader AI ecosystem.

As a member of SII, you'll conduct original and impactful research on improving the security and privacy of frontier intelligence systems. Your goal will be to conduct research that is not only rigorous in theory, but practical enough to improve the systems people rely on every day. This work will be informed by the realities of operating general-purpose AI systems used by millions of people and thousands of enterprises, and you'll be expected to translate both your own research and advances from the broader community to practical improvements that protect and defend Perplexity's users.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Develop threat models for emerging attack surfaces in AI-native products, including browser, search, and autonomous agents.

 - Identify and analyze security and privacy threats across AI systems, infrastructure, and user-facing products.

 - Develop novel defenses, mitigations, and detection mechanisms for security and privacy in AI-native products.

 - Build security evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and datasets to measure the effectiveness of different defense mechanisms.

 - Partner with Perplexity’s Security Engineering team to translate state of the art research into shipped security features and hardened system architectures.

 - Collaborate with top-tier academic and industry researchers in SII's external research network.

 - Publish findings at premier venues and contribute to the broader security research community.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Hold a PhD (or equivalent research experience) in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, with a primary focus on security and/or privacy.

 - Experience publishing at top security conferences (IEEE S&P, USENIX Security, ACM CCS, NDSS) demonstrating original, impactful research contributions.

 - Deep expertise in one or more of: security of agentic systems, systems security, web and applications security, program analysis, and software security.

 - Proficiency in Python (bonus points for TypeScript, Go, and/or Rust).

 - Ability to operate with high independence, willing to dive in and take ownership, and comfortable in a fast-paced environment where research directly informs product.

 - Clear and concise communcation, translating complex attack narratives into actionable insights for engineering and leadership.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, API Platform)
jobs.description:
PERPLEXITY API PLATFORM

Perplexity innovates at the frontier of AI infrastructure, search, and orchestration to serve the world's most discerning users. The Perplexity API Platform brings our technology to the world's most discerning developers. From exabyte-scale knowledge indexes to codegen-first agent runtimes, the building blocks behind Perplexity's applications are some of the most battle-tested AI systems in the industry.

We believe these same building blocks can and should power the aspirations of builders everywhere. It's one thing to solve planet-scale retrieval, long-horizon orchestration, and other foundational AI challenges within a single product ecosystem. The true measure of success is to turn those solutions into elegant APIs that delight developers and agents alike. Our API Platform delivers frontier intelligence to thousands of customers: startups, trillion-dollar enterprises, U.S. and allied governments, and everyone in between.

We've achieved incredible scale, yet we're just getting started. Join us to build tools for curious minds.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

Perplexity is seeking strong engineers with a passion for delivering frontier intelligence and infrastructure to developers. Our company builds technology that reshapes how people search, reason, and interact with the world around them. Week after week, we observe increasing demand for programmatic interfaces to that technology. The API Platform engineering team is charged with designing, implementing, and scaling these interfaces.

As a member of our team, you'll work on an eclectic portfolio spanning distributed systems, performance optimization, agent orchestration, and frontier topics that often change with each passing month. Throughout this work, you'll prioritize great developer and agent experience alike. You'll also define technical strategy for how we scale to meet compounding growth exponentials (number of customers, agents per customer, compute/retrieval per agent, etc.).




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, build, and operate mission-critical APIs that provide our customers the building blocks for frontier intelligence.

 - Own and evolve the API gateway and routing layer: authentication, authorization, rate limiting and quotas, usage metering, and request routing across heterogeneous upstream services.

 - Build the paved road for API services: standardized service scaffolding, container builds, CI/CD, Kubernetes and Helm deployment, and progressive rollouts with fast rollback, so a new API product goes from idea to production in days, not weeks.

 - Build API governance into the platform: contract-first schemas, breaking-change detection in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from a single source of truth.

 - Unify cross-cutting capabilities (billing and usage, rate limiting, organization and identity settings, analytics and observability) so every API product gets them by default instead of rebuilding them.

 - Ensure low latency and high throughput through aggressive performance optimization (including on upstream systems).

 - Harden system security and reliability across heterogeneous compute environments, and operate what you build: SLOs, on-call, and incident response.

 - Collaborate across teams to bring novel frontier capabilities into the API Platform, and partner with infrastructure teams on compute, networking, secrets, and security.

 - Continually reimagine the customer needs of tomorrow (and the architectures to serve those needs), while faithfully serving the customer workloads of today.

 - Uphold engineering excellence through design reviews, code quality, and internal documentation.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 5+ years of backend engineering experience with Python, Go, or Rust, including significant time building platforms or infrastructure used by other engineering teams.

 - Strong understanding of high-traffic API design: schema evolution & versioning, idempotency, authentication

jobs.title: AI Systems Engineer - Data & State Management - Senior
jobs.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

We are seeking an AI Systems Engineer to own the stateful backbone of EY’s AI-native platform, including the data stores, memory tiers, and event streaming systems that hold and move every piece of state in EY’s Hybrid AI Multi-Environment Runtime (HAI). This role ensures that agentic AI workloads have durable, performant, and consistent access to data across cloud, on-prem, edge, client-managed, and air-gapped environments.

Within HAI, this is a distinct discipline from platform operations and model serving. This role owns everything that must remember, persist, or flow: relational and key-value state, vector and graph stores, object storage, durable workflows, and the streaming and change-data-capture pipelines that connect them. It is the layer that makes the platform stateful, reliable, and event-driven.

It is ideal for a data-infrastructure engineer who is equally comfortable operating production databases and high-throughput streaming systems, who treats data durability, consistency, and recoverability as non-negotiable in regulated client contexts, and who understands that state is the hardest part of any distributed platform to get right.

Your Key Responsibilities

• Own the memory and data stores: relational and durable state (PostgreSQL, DBOS durable workflows), caching (Redis/Valkey), vector stores (Qdrant/Milvus/PGVector), knowledge graphs (Neo4j), and object/block storage (MinIO, OpenEBS Mayastor), across every environment and tenant.
• Own event streaming and async messaging: Apache Kafka (Strimzi), NATS JetStream (agent-to-agent), Debezium (change data capture), Apache Flink (stream processing), and Apicurio/CloudEvents (schema and event contracts).
• Own data durability, consistency, and recoverability: replication, backup/restore, point-in-time recovery, and cross-environment data movement, tiered by RPO/RTO.
• Build and operate streaming and CDC pipelines that move data reliably between stores and services, with schema governance and evolution that prevents breaking changes across producers and consumers.
• Make state multi-tenant and portable, ensuring isolation, performance, and consistent semantics whether running on managed cloud services or self-hosted OSS in an air-gapped environment.
• Provide the data and lineage substrate that downstream governance, observability, and AI knowledge capabilities depend on, as well as integrating with lineage tooling.

Skills And Attributes For Success

• Deep expertise operating production databases and data stores at scale, including relational, key-value, vector, graph, and object storage.
• Strong command of streaming and event-driven architectures (Kafka, NATS, CDC, stream processing) and the consistency tradeoffs they involve.
• A durability-first mindset: thinking in terms of consistency, recoverability, blast radius, and data correctness under failure.
• Ability to operate stateful systems consistently across managed cloud and self-hosted OSS in cloud, on-prem, edge, and air-gapped environments.
• Strong grasp of schema governance and evolution, preventing breaking changes across producers and consumers.
• Strong communicator able to guide consuming teams toward the right storage and streaming patterns.
• Orientation toward reliability and toil reduction through automation and infrastructure-as-code for data systems.

To qualify you must have

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or related technical field.
• 8+ years operating production data infrastructure, streaming systems, or database platforms at scale.
• Hands-on expertise with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and caching (Redis/Valkey), including HA, replication, and backup/recovery.
• Exposure to AI/ML data

jobs.title: Research Scientist in Biomedical Data Science
jobs.description:
Description

The Genomic Data Science Core (GDSC), part of the Center for
Quantitative Biology at Dartmouth, is seeking a Research Scientist
to analyze next generation squencing data and provide biological
insight to the results. The GDSC is a fee-for-service
bioinformatics core facility aimed at providing computational
expertise to the Dartmouth faculty in advancing their research
goals. The Research Scientist will work as part of the GDSC team to
analyze high-dimensional genomic datasets. The ability to work
effectively as part of a team is essential to be successful in this
position.

The ideal candidate is expected to have knowledge and/or experience
analyzing large datasets from multiple major genomic modalities
such as RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, WES, WGS, ChIP-seq, and metagenomics.
Experience with other types of genomic data (e.g. methylation/SNP
arrays, TCR-seq, Nanostring) is a plus, and experience with
single-cell or spatial transcriptomics is especially desirable. The
candidate should have familiarity with computational tools used for
these analyses and the ability to write scripts in BASH, R, and/or
Python. Furthermore, the candidate should have a working knowledge
of basic statistical concepts (regression analysis, linear
modeling, probability). Experience with any of the following are
also highly desirable: use of workflow management software (e.g.
Snakemake, Nextflow) to construct and maintain data analysis
pipelines, software management with package managers (e.g. Conda)
or containers (e.g. Singularity or Docker), version control with
Git/GitHub, familiarity with public genomics databases (GEO, SRA,
NCBI, Ensembl), experience with genome browsers (e.g. IGV), high
performance computing systems and/or cloud computing environments
(GCP, AWS).

Researchers at Dartmouth encompass a broad range of biological
disciplines, including cancer biology, immunology, neurology,
microbiology, and environmental science. As such, the candidate
must have a desire to work in a highly collaborative research
environment and possess strong communication and organizational
skills to manage and multitask diverse analysis projects. The
Research Scientist will be responsible for tracking his/her time
committed to each project for billing purposes. Due to the
service-based nature of this role, being able to work to
established deadlines is a crucial requirement. Presenting at
conferences and seminars is encouraged, and opportunities for
career development such as workshops and coursework will be
supported.

Primary Responsibilities

Note: This position is dependent on the availability of sponsored
funding.

• Contribute to experimental design and development of
appropriate data analysis plans.

• Perform genomic data analysis for core users.

• Establish and maintain an open line of communication with users
working to deadlines and specifications outlined in the analysis
plan.

• Provide clear and detailed analysis summary reports to core
users.

• Develop and maintain genomic data analysis pipelines and
workflows.

• Use RADAR for analysis time and fee tracking.

• Work in a collaboratively and participate in team meetings as
well as meetings with core users.

• Provide scientific training and mentoring to other core members
or core users where required.

• Assist in the preparation of publications and grant
proposals.

• Become familiar with all services offered and serve as a point
of contact for users.

• Present at local, regional, and national meetings to expand the
visibility of the core.

• Engage in professional development opportunities such as
workshops and courses to acquire new skills.

• Performs other duties as required.

Minimum Qualifications

• Proficiency with BASH and R or Python.

• Proven organizational skills with exceptional attention to
detail.

• Ability to work independently, taking initiative to advance
projects.

• Demonstrated experience analyzing next generation sequencing
